rows.reasoning: The only evidence is Marsh's No vote on SB1828 (2021), a bill titled "omnibus; taxation" that amends dozens of unrelated statutes — income tax rates, unemployment benefit amounts, class one assessed valuation, urban revenue sharing, forest-product credits and fire district levies. Under the vote ladder a No vote on a multi-subject bill proves nothing, because she may have objected to any part, so it cannot establish "Significantly raise taxes on wealthy people and large companies to fund more public services" or any other rung. No surviving passage supports a chair.
